passage: The French society of the late 18th century was strictly divided into three estates, where the burden of taxation fell almost exclusively on the Third Estate. While the clergy and nobility enjoyed privileges by birth, the Third Estate paid direct taxes like the taille to the state and indirect taxes on everyday items. The Estates General functioned under a system where each estate held one collective vote, rather than individual voting. When the King faced a severe economic crisis, he attempted to increase taxes, but the Third Estate demanded a change in voting procedures. During the revolution, the Jacobins emerged not as nobles, but as a political club of less prosperous members of society. Their rise led to the Reign of Terror, a period defined by strict government-led executions rather than random street violence. Furthermore, the storming of the Bastille was a symbolic act of defiance against royal despotism, even though the prison held only seven inmates at the time. While the revolution promised liberty, it did not immediately grant women the right to vote, nor did it permanently end slavery, which was later reinstated by Napoleon. These events show that the path to democracy was complex and often contradictory, as revolutionary leaders struggled to balance radical ideals with the harsh realities of governance and power.

items.evidence: The Estates General functioned under a system where each estate held one collective vote, rather than individual voting.
items.q: The Third Estate has far more people than the clergy. How does this affect its vote?
options: It still gets only one vote, like each other estate
It gets more votes because it has more people
It gets more votes because it pays more taxes
It gets one vote for each of its leaders
items.explain: Each estate held one collective vote, so the Third Estate's larger size gave it no extra votes.

wrong.why: thinks every individual person had a vote
links voting power to the amount of tax paid
invents a vote per leader from nearby ideas

items.evidence: Their rise led to the Reign of Terror, a period defined by strict government-led executions rather than random street violence.
items.q: How was the Reign of Terror different from simple rioting by the poor?
options: The government itself carried out the executions
The poor carried out the executions in the streets
The nobles carried out the executions in secret
The King carried out the executions in person
items.explain: The Terror was marked by strict government-led executions, not random street violence by the poor.

wrong.why: thinks the Terror was lawless rioting by the poor
thinks Jacobins were nobles acting for themselves
mixes up the King with the revolutionary government

items.evidence: Furthermore, the storming of the Bastille was a symbolic act of defiance against royal despotism, even though the prison held only seven inmates at the time.
items.q: Why is the storming of the Bastille remembered, though it held few prisoners?
options: It showed people's defiance of the King's rule
It freed hundreds of political prisoners at last
It ended slavery in all the French colonies
It gave women the right to vote in France
items.explain: The storming was a symbolic act of defiance against royal despotism, not a rescue of many prisoners.

wrong.why: thinks the prison was full of political prisoners
mixes it up with the later abolition of slavery
mixes it up with women's voting rights

items.evidence: While the revolution promised liberty, it did not immediately grant women the right to vote, nor did it permanently end slavery, which was later reinstated by Napoleon.
items.q: Which fact shows that Napoleon did not fully carry on the revolution's ideals?
options: He brought back slavery after it was ended
He gave women the right to vote
He ended the privileges of the three estates
He ended slavery for good in the colonies
items.explain: Slavery was later reinstated by Napoleon, which went against the revolution's promise of liberty.

wrong.why: thinks women won the vote soon after the revolution
thinks Napoleon was a democratic leader

items.evidence: During the revolution, the Jacobins emerged not as nobles, but as a political club of less prosperous members of society.
items.q: Which group of people formed the Jacobin club?
options: Less wealthy members of French society
Rich nobles who wanted to change laws
Clergy who gave up their old privileges
Royal officers who served the King's court
items.explain: The Jacobins were a political club of less prosperous members of society, not nobles.

wrong.why: assumes reformers came from the First Estate
